jobs.prompt: Use case precise-object-edit. Edit image 1 into a more readable, realistic SQUARE B2B product catalogue hero. Keep this same single horizontal foil bubble insulation roll on a kraft paper core, the same roll width/diameter ratio, the same scale and 3/4 viewpoint. Increase the natural continuous turn-back of the loose sheet at the front-right so buyers can clearly see ONE transparent rounded air-bubble reverse over the same single silver reflective facing. This is ONE continuous laminated sheet, not detached swatches or a second roll. The broad roll surface and sheet flat part show the thin reflective silver face; folded-back corner shows clear polymer domed bubbles with soft specular rims and silver backing seen THROUGH them. Natural thin laminate edges, no foam and no thick padded layer. Image 2 is a company generic reflective-material texture reference ONLY, not evidence of the completed product. Match a practical camera photo with soft diffuse daylight, restrained irregular reflections, gentle contact shadow and slight natural roll-edge imperfections. Seamless uniform #F6F6F4 background. Product complete, centered, 10–12% clear margins, one square image. Keep core construction and original identity. No text, logos, symbols, measurement labels, additional props, detached layers, checkerboard background or collage.

Use case precise-object-edit. Replace the two disconnected rectangular swatches in image 1 with ONE continuous rectangular sample of the SAME foil bubble insulation laminate as image 2. SQUARE close-up product photograph on seamless #F6F6F4. One strip lies foil face up across the lower-left and makes a gentle rounded 180-degree return bend across the middle; the upper-right portion of THE SAME strip is folded back so that its clear air-bubble reverse faces the camera. Keep the return bend and both long side edges visibly continuous, so it is unmistakably the front and back of ONE sample. Single thin silver reflective facing bonded to clear polymer round air cells; silver backing is visible through the translucent domes, with real specular rims. The foil face has very subtle shallow cell impressions and ordinary fine metal creases, not a diamond textile weave. No white foam, no peeling apart bonded layers, no giant bubbles, no pile of layers or separate sample. Natural gravity, only modest rounded curl height. Sample fills ~75% of the square with all edges safely inside frame. Soft daylight, realistic metal and clear plastic, gentle shadows. No labels, arrows, rulers, logos or text.

Use case precise-object-edit. Improve image 1 as one SQUARE photorealistic B2B hero of the SAME proposed passive reflective IBC cover. Preserve exact cuboid tank/cage size and proportions, black plastic pallet, THREE visible front fork pockets, silver flexible cover, existing large rectangular top access flap and small centered bottom front access flap, and overall 3/4 viewpoint. Show BOTH existing flaps opened naturally: top flap hinged at its rear bound edge and folded back onto the top, exposing the black screw cap on a pale translucent closed plastic tank and a small amount of its galvanised cage rails through the existing opening; lower flap folds UP at its existing top hinge, exposing the same tank's small closed outlet valve above the pallet. Fit the cover close to the actual cage with subtle slack at corners, hem wholly above the fork pockets. Do not add a free-standing support, hoses, heater, electronics, new pockets, straps, a new closure type or any extra fittings. Use softer more irregular foil reflections with thin small creases and broad shallow folds instead of the uniform highly crumpled metallic shell. Image 2 is ONLY a general reflective material texture reference. Keep original binding locations and single continuous top and side panels, realistic stitched/bound flap lips, plausible clearance for fingers and the closed valve. Ordinary soft daylight catalogue photo, seamless #F6F6F4 floor/backdrop, entire pallet and cover visible with 10–12% margin and grounded soft shadow. No text, capacity/temperature ratings, logos, water, people, arrows or measurement annotations.

Improve natural flexible laminate drape, a few small crease lines, believable fine foil sheen and contact shadows. Replace the overly uniform exaggerated crinkles with restrained irregular small folds; no silver fabric/satin weave or thick inflated padding. Image 2 is a general reflective material texture reference only. Entire wheeled cage complete, centered with 10–12% safe margin, #F6F6F4 seamless background, practical soft-lit photographic quality. Cartons remain reasonable scale and below cage top. Do not add loose straps, handles, zippers, pockets, people, branding, text, arrows or dimensional claims.

Use case product-mockup. Create a SINGLE SQUARE macro catalogue photograph of ONE rectangular cut sample of the same single-face foil bubble wrap shown in the supplied product reference. A flat rectangle lies on a #F6F6F4 surface with the silver reflective facing UP. Only its TOP-RIGHT CORNER is folded diagonally INWARD across the rest of that same rectangle, like turning down the corner of a page. This folded triangular corner reveals the translucent round-bubble BACK of the same material. A clear diagonal crease connects the triangle with the flat rectangle. The triangle physically overlaps and casts a small contact shadow onto the flat silver surface. This MUST look like a simple page-corner fold, with two of the folded corner's outside edges freely visible above the underlying sheet. Same small round cell diameter and pitch on BOTH sides, perspective-consistent; the domes have clear plastic rims and silver backing seen through them. Preserve ONE bonded laminate throughout. No change in material halfway across a flat sheet, no long S bend, no two separate pieces, no peeled-apart layers, no thick foam. Real thin flexible edge, restrained foil sheen, irregular little creases. Entire rectangle at a modest three-quarter angle with all its corners inside the central 80% of the canvas. Soft daylight and gentle grounded shadow. No roll, no text, logos, rulers, arrows or other props. Purpose is to show front and back of ONE continuous sample.
